name: Example: Finding an Orthogonal Basis For the Column Space of a Matrix
problem:
Consider the subspace $\textrm{Col}(A)$ and an orthogonal basis $\mathcal B$ of $\textrm{Col}(A),$ where $A$ and $\mathcal B$ are given below. Given that $\mathcal B$ is derived from $\textrm{Col}(A)$ using the Gram-Schmidt process, what is the value of $\dfrac{c}{a}?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070290/assets/9af89cb1c6f57895919cfec30701a6aa0da76adafcae91a0636b1e7ee3a89e1a.png)
worked_solution:
Recall that $\textrm{Col}(A)$ is the span of the columns of $A.$  

First, let's denote

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070290/assets/fc5495a909acfddca53e63d336f5d7c2261ee6df626f9db2ab9fe4f9714a3198.png)

We proceed to find an orthogonal basis using the Gram-Schmidt process, as follows.

- **Step 1**: We set ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070290/assets/8db4c83e14f998397313580b16662b9c80e44bda34da21e8bf92b4a4e1d89ab8.png)

- **Step 2**: Next, we find $\mathbf{v}_2$, by using the formula

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{{a}_{2}\cdot {v}_{1}}{{v}_{1}\cdot {v}_{1}}{v}_{1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the formula for $\mathbf v_2$ in our case gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{v}_{2} & ={a}_{2}-\frac{(-5)\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-2)+(-3)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{2}^{2}}{v}_{1} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5 \\ -1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -3 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070290/assets/061b35426271be433b6f2a92dd3e189edfd3a725dd0fac17cb865a4984c0911d.png) is an orthogonal basis for $\textrm{Col}(A).$

Finally, $a=-4,$ $c=-1,$ and  

$$
\dfrac{c}{a} = \dfrac{-1}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{4}.
$$
